documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary - Orthopedic Surgery
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 07/07/2025  Discharged: 07/17/2025
Service: Orthopaedic Surgery (Hospital Medicine and Vascular Surgery consulting)
Patient: Sandra Kendall, 68F

Allergies at discharge: HEPARIN (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia - all heparin products including LMWH and flushes). Sulfa (rash).

Principal procedure: Right total hip arthroplasty, 07/07/2025. Uncomplicated intraoperatively.

Discharge diagnoses:
1. Right hip osteoarthritis, s/p right THA
2. Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
3. Acute arterial thrombosis, left femoral artery
4. Atrial fibrillation on chronic warfarin
5. Hypertension; hyperlipidemia

Hospital course: Warfarin had been held from 07/01 with an enoxaparin bridge from 07/03, resumed after surgery. On post-operative day 3 (07/10) she reported new pain in the left foot. The foot was pale and cool with diminished dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses. Platelets had fallen from 240 K/uL on admission to 80 K/uL. PT and aPTT were normal. Arterial duplex showed thrombus in the left femoral artery. HIT was suspected; all heparin was stopped and an argatroban infusion begun. PF4/heparin antibody ELISA returned positive (OD 1.84). Vascular surgery evaluated and recommended anticoagulation without operative intervention. Foot pain and pallor resolved and pedal pulses were again palpable by 07/14. Warfarin was restarted at 5 mg once platelets recovered above 150 K, overlapped with argatroban until INR therapeutic.

At discharge: platelets 168 K/uL, INR 2.6. Hip incision clean, weight bearing as tolerated with walker. Left foot warm, pulses palpable.

Discharge medications: warfarin 5 mg nightly (INR goal 2-3), metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, calcium carbonate/vitamin D twice daily, acetaminophen as needed. Enoxaparin discontinued.

Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks for CBC and INR. Orthopaedics at 6 weeks. HEPARIN ALLERGY TO BE ADDED TO ALL RECORDS; avoid all heparin products lifelong.

Dictated by Hospital Medicine for Orthopaedic Surgery. Faxed 08/20/2025.

documents.title: Post-discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called, home since yesterday afternoon. Hip went fine but she says on day 3 her left foot went cold and white and they found a clot in the leg artery - told her it was from a reaction to the blood thinner shots, platelets dropped. Was on an IV blood thinner, now back on warfarin 5 mg. Foot feels normal now. Using walker, home PT starting Monday. No discharge paperwork in our system yet - asked her to bring her packet. Post-discharge visit with PCP booked 7/24, CBC and INR then. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Discharged 7/17 after R THA 7/7. Contact made 7/18.

Per patient (summary not yet received; she forgot the packet): on post-op day 3 her left foot turned pale and painful, platelet count had dropped, a clot was found in the left femoral artery, and she was told it was heparin-induced thrombocytopenia from the enoxaparin. Treated with an IV non-heparin anticoagulant, no surgery on the leg. Back on warfarin 5 mg before discharge.

Today: hip sore but improving, walker in the house, cane outside. Home PT twice a week. Left foot normal - no pain, no color change, no numbness. No bleeding, no calf pain, no chest pain or dyspnea.

Exam: incision R lateral hip healing, staples out, no erythema. L foot warm, normal color, DP and PT pulses 2+ bilaterally. No calf tenderness. Irregular rhythm, rate controlled. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. HIT with L femoral arterial thrombosis, July 2025 - foot recovered. Problem list updated. She must never receive heparin of any kind; told her to say so at every visit, ER and pharmacy. CBC today to confirm platelet recovery.
2. AF on warfarin - INR today, then weekly x2 given recent restart.
3. s/p R THA - PT, ortho follow-up at 6 weeks.
4. Records request to hospital for discharge summary.

Joint Replacement Clinic
Patient: Sandra Kendall  DOB 04/10/1957
Allergies: Heparin (HIT), Sulfa (rash)

Now 3 months out from a successful right THA. Left knee pain has become the limiting problem: medial and anterior pain with stairs, standing and getting up from a chair, stiffness after sitting. Acetaminophen partially helps.

Exam: mild varus, no effusion. ROM 5-110 degrees with crepitus. Ligaments stable. Neurovascularly intact.
Radiographs (standing AP, lateral, sunrise): advanced osteoarthritis of the left knee, medial joint space loss with osteophytes.

Impression: end-stage left knee osteoarthritis.

Plan: she wishes to proceed with left total knee arthroplasty. Tentatively scheduled for 01/08/2026. Medical pre-operative evaluation with her PCP in December. Perioperative anticoagulation plan to follow from our pre-admission team.

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP EVAL - L TKA planned 1/8/2026 (outside orthopedics)

History notable for HIT with left femoral arterial thrombosis after an enoxaparin bridge for her R THA in July 2025 (PF4 antibody positive). Fully recovered.

No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations or edema. Walks 20-30 min on level ground, limited by the knee. Tolerated anesthesia in July.

Meds: warfarin 5 mg, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, calcium/D, acetaminophen prn.
ALLERGIES: HEPARIN - HIT (all heparins incl. enoxaparin and flushes). Sulfa - rash.

Exam: irregularly irregular, controlled. Lungs clear. No edema. R hip incision healed. L knee crepitus, mild varus.
ECG 6/2025 unchanged rhythm; not repeated.

Assessment: medically acceptable risk for L TKA.

Recommendations to surgical team:
1. NO HEPARIN PRODUCTS of any kind - prior HIT with thrombosis. No LMWH bridge. If anticoagulant prophylaxis is needed before INR is therapeutic, use a non-heparin agent.
2. Warfarin hold per surgeon; given the HIT history I would not bridge.
3. Continue metoprolol; hold lisinopril morning of surgery.

Faxed to orthopedic pre-admission testing with today's labs.
